# Adjudication Task — Chapter 576

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃576화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|달칵.
  6|
  7|짧은 통화가 끝났다. 스마트폰에서 흘러나오던 신호음은 멈췄지만, 귓가로 올라간 손은 쉽게 내려가지 않았다.
  8|
  9|최민우는 갈등 어린 눈빛으로 청와대 관저 앞에 펼쳐진 녹지원(綠地園)을 가로질렀다.
 10|
 11|처음과 달리 느려진 발걸음은 머릿속을 가득 메운 어떤 생각 때문이었다.
 12|
 13|‘송천우가 나를 만나고자 한다. 그것도 지금 당장.’
 14|
 15|송천우. 아레스 길드라는 철옹성으로 자신을 들여보내 줄 트로이의 목마.
 16|
 17|그의 연락을 기다린 것은 사실이지만, 하필 오늘. 그것도 당장 만나자고 할 줄은 몰랐다.
 18|
 19|최민우는 짧았던 통화 내용을 떠올리며 내심 중얼거렸다.
 20|
 21|‘어떻게 해야 할까.’
 22|
 23|그때, 최민우의 발걸음이 우뚝 멈췄다.
 24|
 25|어느덧 그의 앞에는 두 갈래 길이 펼쳐져 있었다. 마치 마음에 생겨난 또 하나의 갈림길처럼.
 26|
 27|‘부산. 그리고 송천우.’
 28|
 29|시간이 없다. 선택해야 한다. 깊게 가라앉은 눈빛으로 두 갈래 길을 응시하던 최민우는 마침내 발걸음을 뗐다.
 30|
 31|사박, 추위에 얼어붙은 잔디가 구두 굽 아래에서 바스라졌다. 비록 두 갈래로 나뉘었지만 결국 모든 길은 출구로 통했다.
 32|
 33|청와대 경호실과 붙어 있는 정문 밖에는 이미 낯익은 얼굴이 그를 기다리고 있었다.
 34|
 35|“도련님.”
 36|
 37|김 집사를 향해 눈인사를 건넨 최민우는 정문을 나섰다.
 38|
 39|길가에는 잘 빠진 리무진 한 대와 검은색 SUV 다섯 대. 그리고 이십여 명의 헌터가 기다리고 있었다.
 40|
 41|이제 상당한 규모를 자랑하는 평화 길드 내에서도 정예라 불리기에 손색이 없는 실력자들.
 42|
 43|이미 착용하고 있는 갖가지 장비는 만반의 전투태세를 갖추었다는 증거다.
 44|
 45|이어 들려온 김 집사의 한 마디는 짐작을 확신으로 바꿔주었다.
 46|
 47|“모셔 가기 위해 대기 중이었습니다.”
 48|
 49|“미안합니다. 자리가 자리인지라 미처 확인하지 못했군요. 그보다 진태경 씨가 네임드 몬스터를 처치했다고 들었는데, 현재 상황은?”
 50|
 51|“말씀하신 대로 이번 웨이브로 등장한 네임드 몬스터인 크라켄은 제거되었고, 약 일천 개체가 넘는 머맨(Merman)이 해운대와 광안리로 퍼져 나간 상황입니다.”
 52|
 53|김 집사의 대답을 들은 최민우가 낮게 뇌까렸다.
 54|
 55|“피해가 극심하겠군요.”
 56|
 57|비록 서울만큼은 아니지만, 부산은 대한민국 제2의 도시라는 이름에 걸맞게 오백만에 달하는 인구를 보유한 대도시.
 58|
 59|최근 마력 상승에 힘입어 더욱 강해진 몬스터가 그런 곳에 천 마리나 등장했다는 것은 말 그대로 재앙이다.
 60|
 61|하지만 김 집사는 침착하게 고개를 저었다.
 62|
 63|“기뻐해야 할 일은 아니지만…… 다행히 사상자의 숫자는 예상했던 수치보다 극히 적습니다.”
 64|
 65|“진태경 씨가 크라켄을 처치했다고 해도, 일천이나 되는 머맨을 모두 막을 수는 없을 텐데요.”
 66|
 67|“스켈, 아니. 스톤 킹이 있었습니다.”
 68|
 69|“아.”
 70|
 71|언제나 오만하고 자신만만한 표정을 짓는 금발 외국인의 얼굴이 눈앞을 스친다. 최민우는 작은 탄성과 함께 고개를 끄덕였다.
 72|
 73|‘그가 있다면 가능하지.’
 74|
 75|몬스터와 미국인 사이에서 정체성 혼란을 겪고 있는 언데드 몬스터의 존재는 극소수에게만 허락된 비밀.
 76|
 77|그리고 최민우는 그가 결코 S급 헌터에 뒤떨어지지 않는 강자라는 사실 역시 알고 있었다.
 78|
 79|“예. 다행히 그 두 분의 활약 덕분에 피해 규모는 그리 크지 않습니다.”
 80|
 81|천운이라고 할 수밖에 없다. 진태경과 스켈레톤 킹은 일인군단(一人群團)이라 부르기에 부족함이 없는 강자들이니까.
 82|
 83|게다가 지닌 바 능력에 비해 여러 가지 제약이 있는 스켈레톤 킹과 달리, 진태경은 대한민국. 아니 전 세계에서도 최고로 꼽히는 실력자다.
 84|
 85|‘……한 사람을 제외하고는, 말이지.’
 86|
 87|내심 중얼거린 최민우가 입을 열었다.
 88|
 89|“그보다 우리 평화 길드는?”
 90|
 91|“약 5분 전, 긴급 구조팀 및 준비되어 있던 세 개 팀을 부산으로 파견했습니다. 부산에 위치한 길드와 휘하 헌터들은 물론, 외부 지원군도 전력을 다해 피해 확산을 막는 중입니다.”
 92|
 93|국내에 존재하는 게이트와 각 지방의 길드 및 헌터 숫자를 줄줄이 꿰고 있는 최민우다.
 94|
 95|몇 번 눈동자를 깜빡인 것으로 계산을 끝마친 그가 불쑥 입을 열었다.
 96|
 97|“적어도 두 시간 안에 진압 완료. 맞습니까?”
 98|
 99|“그렇습니다. 물론 진압 후에도 피해자 구출 및 시간이 많이 소요되겠지만…….”
100|
101|“그럼 현재 상황으로서는 진태경 씨나 스톤 킹의 호출은 무리겠군요.”
102|
103|“실례지만 도련님, 호출이라니 그게 무슨.”
104|
105|“아닙니다. 출발합시다.”
106|
107|그러나 나직하게 끊어 내는 말과 달리, 리무진으로 걸음을 옮기는 최민우의 입술은 달싹이고 있었다.
108|
109|이제는 메시지 마법이 아닌, 전음(傳音)이라 불려야 마땅할 그것이 김 집사의 귓가를 파고든다.
110|
111|- 그가 만남을 요청해 왔습니다.
112|
113|“……!”
114|
115|김 집사의 눈동자가 잘게 흔들렸다. 이름을 말하지 않아도 ‘그’가 누구를 지칭하는 것인지는, 충분히 알아들을 수 있었다.
116|
117|- 송천우가 말입니까?
118|
119|- 네.
120|
121|- 도련님. 위험할지도 모릅니다. 어차피 부산 몬스터 웨이브도 마무리 중이니 차라리 길드 하우스로…….
122|
123|- 제 외할아버님의 신변에 관한 이야기를 하더군요. 석고준이 함정을 파고 있다는 이야기도 함께.
124|
125|딱딱하게 굳은 김 집사의 얼굴을 바라본 최민우가 조용히 전음을 이었다.
126|
127|- 그를 만나야겠습니다. 지금 당장.
128|
129|
130|
131|* * *
132|
133|
134|
135|강원도 평창에 위치한 B급 게이트, [예티의 겨울 산맥]은 헌터들에게 있어 그리 매력적인 레이드 장소는 아니었다.
136|
137|제아무리 뛰어난 신체 능력에 마법 장비가 있다고는 해도, 발이 푹푹 꺼지는 설산(雪山)에서 털북숭이 거인들과 싸우는 건 썩 유쾌한 일이 아니니까.
138|
139|하지만 그렇다고 해서 모두가 [예티의 겨울 산맥]을 기피하는 것은 아니었다.
140|
141|최근 잇따라 마력이 상승하는 상황 속에서도 그곳을 찾는 헌터들은 존재했고, 지금 막 리프트를 타고 내려온 일단의 무리 역시 그런 축에 속했다.
142|
143|“젠장. 갑자기 출입 금지라니.”
144|
145|“그러게요. 근데 팀장님. 저희 오늘 수당 나와요?”
146|
147|“……예티보다 더한 놈일세, 이거. 마력 상승 때문에 게이트 진입도 못 했는데 수당은 개뿔이. 양심에 털 났어?”
148|
149|“에이. 괜히 기대했네. 그런데 위에 있던 사람들은 누구예요? 마스크 쓰고 있던 잘생긴 남자는 좀 눈에 익은 것 같기도 하고.”
150|
151|“모르지. 그걸 내가 어떻게 알…… 응?”
152|
153|투덜거리며 내려오는 삼십여 명의 헌터들. 그중 선두에서 걸어가고 있던 팀장이 문득 눈을 동그랗게 떴다.
154|
155|그의 시선 끝에, 빠르지도 느리지도 않은 걸음으로 길을 올라오는 한 사람이 있었다.
156|
157|“쯧쯧. 저 양반도 허탕치겠구만.”
158|
159|척 보아하니 저 사람도 레이드를 위해 온 것이 분명하다. 팀장은 40대쯤으로 보이는 중년인에게 말을 걸었다.
160|
161|“예티. 레이드?”
162|
163|불쑥 던진 두 단어에, 순간 멈칫한 중년인이 말없이 고개를 끄덕였다. 작게 혀를 찬 팀장이 말을 이었다.
164|
165|“사장님 쪽도 오늘 허탕이시네. 올라가지 마세요. 위에 막혔습니다.”
166|
167|“…….”
168|
169|“뭐 갑자기 마력 수치가 상승했다나 뭐라나. 여하튼 출입 금지래요. 우리도 지금 그것 때문에 빠꾸 친 거고.”
170|
171|“…….”
172|
173|“……저기요? 제 얘기 못 들으셨어요?”
174|
175|이상함을 느낀 팀장이 눈살을 찌푸린 그때, 한마디 대꾸도 없이 이야기만 듣고 있던 중년인이 그들을 슥 지나쳤다.
176|
177|저벅. 저벅.
178|
179|멀어져 가는 중년인의 모습에, 팀장이 중얼거렸다.
180|
181|“뭐야, 저 인간?”
182|
183|하지만 팀장의 호의는 중년인에게 있어 쓸데없는 참견에 불과했다.
184|
185|덜컹.
186|
187|작은 흔들림과 함께 리프트를 타고 올라간 그는 자신을 기다리고 있던 수십 쌍의 시선을 발견할 수 있었다.
188|
189|그중 상당한 수준으로 보이는 헌터가 불청객을 막아섰다.
190|
191|“죄송하지만, 마력 수치 상승으로 인하여 게이트에 진입할 수 없…….”
192|
193|“제 손님입니다.”
194|
195|순간 들려온 나직한 목소리에, 벽처럼 서 있던 이십여 명의 헌터들이 좌우로 길을 텄다.
196|
197|그리고 그들이 만들어 낸 길의 끝에는 두 사람이 있었다.
198|
199|“늦으셨군요.”
200|
201|최민우의 고저 없는 목소리에 환영 마법으로 모습을 바꾼 중년인, 송천우는 꾹 다물고 있던 입술을 뗐다.
202|
203|“조심해야 했으니까. 그리고 이 장소도 민우 네가 정한 것이 아니냐.”
204|
205|“먼저 게이트에서 만나자고 한 사람은 제가 아닙니다. 그렇다면 장소 정도는 제가 정해도 상관없겠죠.”
206|
207|“도청이나 혹시 모를 감시를 피하기 위해서는 어쩔 수 없었다. 게이트 안으로 들어가면 모두 무용지물이니.”
208|
209|“그럼 문제없겠군요. 이 게이트는 평화 길드 소유입니다. 서로 조심하기에 적격인 곳이죠.”
210|
211|“……서로? 날 의심한다는 뜻이냐?”
212|
213|송천우의 물음에 대답한 것은 최민우가 아닌, 그 뒤에 조용히 서 있던 김 집사였다.
214|
215|“그럼 도련님이 도대체 어떤 이유로 당신을 믿어야 합니까?”
216|
217|“이보게. 화종이.”
218|
219|“함부로 제 이름을 부르지 마십시오. 우리 관계는 이미 오래전에 끝났습니다.”
220|
221|“……!”
222|
223|빙하처럼 차가운 눈빛에 송천우의 눈꺼풀이 파르르 떨렸다.
224|
225|한때는 호형호제하던 시절도 있었지만, 충성과 야망이라는 갈림길에서 헤어진 그들이다.
226|
227|두 사람 사이에 싸늘한 냉기가 내려앉은 그때, 나직한 목소리가 울려 퍼졌다.
228|
229|“그보다 먼저 나눠야 할 이야기가 있는 것으로 압니다만.”
230|
231|부드럽지만 핵심을 찌르는 한 마디.
232|
233|동시에 물러난 두 사람을 번갈아 바라본 최민우가 돌아섰다. 마력장이 일렁이는 게이트 입구가 그곳에 있었다.
234|
235|“두 분은 저와 함께 게이트 안으로. 다른 길드원들은 혹시 모를 외부의 침입을 차단할 겁니다.”
236|
237|최민우가 가장 먼저 걸음을 내디뎠고, 김 집사와 송천우가 뒤를 따랐다.
238|
239|쏴아아악.
240|
241|서늘하고 끈적한 마력이 전신을 감싼다. 다시 눈을 떴을 때, 세 사람의 눈앞에는 온통 새하얗게 물든 세상이 펼쳐져 있었다.
242|
243|예티의 겨울 산맥.
244|
245|사방을 가득 채운 눈더미, 가파른 경사를 지닌 그곳 어디에선가 몬스터의 괴성이 울려 퍼졌다.
246|
247|- 콰우우우우!
248|
249|그러나 세 사람은 혹한의 추위와 소름 끼치는 괴성에도 무덤덤했다.
250|
251|한낱 예티에게 겁을 먹기에는 그들의 수준이 너무 높았고, 그보다 앞서 이곳을 찾은 이유는 레이드가 아닌 밀담(密談)을 나누기 위해서였으니까.
252|

[P36]
*Except for one person…*

[P37]

[P38]

[P40]
“Yes. Of course, rescuing the victims afterward will take considerable time as well…”

[P41]
“Then we can’t call Mr. Jin Taekyung or the Stone King away under the circumstances.”

[P42]
“Forgive me, Young Master, but call them away for what?”

[P43]
“Never mind. Let’s go.”

[P44]
Choi’s reply was quiet and final, but his lips moved again as he walked toward the limousine.

[P45]

[P46]
—He’s asked to meet me.

[P47]
“……!”

[P48]
Butler Kim’s eyes trembled. Choi had not named him, but there was no mistaking who *he* meant.

[P49]
—Song Cheonwoo?

[P50]
—Yes.

[P51]
—Young Master, it may be dangerous. The Busan Monster Wave is already nearing its end. We could go back to the Guild House instead—

[P52]
—He spoke about my maternal grandfather’s safety. And about a trap Go Jun is setting.

[P53]
Choi watched Butler Kim’s face go rigid and continued quietly.

[P54]
—I have to meet him. Right now.

[P55]
* * *

[P56]
The B-rank Gate in Pyeongchang, Gangwon Province, known as *Yeti’s Winter Range*, was not an especially appealing raid site.

[P57]

[P58]
Still, not everyone avoided *Yeti’s Winter Range*. Some Hunters continued to visit despite the recent, repeated rises in magic power. The group that had just ridden the lift down was among them.

[P59]
“Damn it. No entry, all of a sudden?”

[P60]
“Right? Hey, Team Leader, are we getting paid for today?”

[P61]
“……You’re worse than a yeti. We couldn’t even get into the Gate because the magic power went up, and you’re asking about pay? Have you got no shame?”

[P62]
“Aw, there goes my money. Anyway, who were those people up there? That good-looking guy in the mask seemed kind of familiar.”

[P63]
“Beats me. How would I know—huh?”

[P64]
The thirty-odd Hunters came down the path grumbling. Their Team Leader, walking at the front, suddenly widened his eyes.

[P65]
A man was walking up toward them at an unhurried pace.

[P66]
“Tsk. Looks like he’s going to come away empty-handed too.”

[P67]
The man had obviously come for a raid. The Team Leader called out to him. He looked to be in his forties.

[P68]
“Yeti raid?”

[P69]
The middle-aged man paused at the abrupt question, then nodded without a word.

[P70]
The Team Leader clicked his tongue. “Then you’re out of luck too, Boss. Don’t bother going up. They’ve closed it off.”

[P71]
“……”

[P72]
“Magic power reading went up suddenly, or something. Anyway, no one’s allowed in. That’s why we’re heading back.”

[P73]
“……”

[P74]
“……Hello? Did you hear me?”

[P75]
The Team Leader frowned. The man had listened to everything without saying a word, and now he simply walked past them.

[P76]
*Step. Step.*

[P77]
“What’s with that guy?” the Team Leader muttered as the man receded up the path.

[P78]
To the middle-aged man, however, the warning was nothing but needless meddling.

[P79]
*Clatter.*

[P80]
The lift carried him up with a slight jolt. At the top, dozens of pairs of eyes turned toward him.

[P81]
A Hunter who looked quite capable stepped forward to bar his way.

[P82]
“Sorry, but due to the rise in the magic power reading, you can’t enter the Gate—”

[P83]
“He’s my guest.”

[P84]
At the quiet voice, the twenty-odd Hunters standing like a wall parted to let him through.

[P85]
Two people stood at the end of the path they made.

[P86]
“You’re late.”

[P87]
The middle-aged man—Song Cheonwoo, his appearance changed by an illusion spell—finally spoke at Choi Minwoo’s flat greeting.

[P88]
“I had to be careful. And you were the one who chose this place, Minwoo.”

[P89]
“I wasn’t the one who suggested meeting at a Gate. Surely that gave me the right to choose which one.”

[P90]
“We had to avoid wiretapping and any other surveillance. None of it will work once we’re inside.”

[P91]
“Then there should be no problem. This Gate belongs to the Peace Guild. It’s a suitable place for both of us to be cautious.”

[P92]
“……Both of us? You suspect me?”

[P93]
It was Butler Kim, standing quietly behind Choi, who answered.

[P94]
“Why should the Young Master trust you?”

[P95]
“Come now, Hwa-jong.”

[P96]
“Do not call me by my name. Whatever relationship we had ended long ago.”

[P97]
“……!”

[P98]
Song Cheonwoo’s eyelids trembled at Butler Kim’s glacial stare.

[P99]

[P100]
As the chill settled between them, Choi spoke.

[P101]
“I believe there’s something more important we need to discuss first.”

[P102]
The words were gentle, but they cut to the point. Both men backed down. Choi glanced from one to the other, then turned toward the Gate entrance, where a field of magic power shimmered.

[P103]
“You two will come inside with me. The other Guild members will keep anyone else from entering.”

[P104]
Choi went first. Butler Kim and Song Cheonwoo followed.

[P105]
*Whoooooosh.*

[P106]
Cold, sticky magic power enveloped them. When they opened their eyes again, a world of white stretched before them.

[P107]
*Yeti’s Winter Range.*

[P108]
Snowdrifts lay in every direction across its steep slopes. Somewhere in the mountains, a monster roared.

[P109]
—Kraaaaaaaar!

[P110]
The three men remained unmoved by the bitter cold and the chilling cry. They were far too powerful to fear a mere yeti. Besides, they had come for a private conversation, not a raid.

[P111]
“Tell me about my maternal grandfather’s safety,” Choi said. “And the trap Go Jun is preparing.”

[P112]
Song gave a bitter smile at the direct demand.

[P113]
“I haven’t seen much of you over the years, but… you haven’t changed.”

[P114]
“Just get to the point. I don’t think I’m asking much.”

[P115]
Song let out a shallow breath. White mist rose into the wind as he spoke, his voice sounding older than before.

[P116]
“Would you walk with me a little? I’d like to speak to you alone.”

[P117]
Butler Kim frowned. Choi answered evenly.

[P118]
“Is that necessary?”

[P119]
“You still suspect me.”

[P120]
“I still have no reason to trust you.”

[P121]
“This Gate belongs to the Peace Guild, not to me or Ares. You chose it yourself. How could I have set a trap here?”

[P122]
“……”

[P123]
“I’m not stupid enough to try something against my only ally.”

[P124]
Choi had been looking out across the snowy mountains. He turned and studied Song’s eyes. They did not waver in the slightest.

[P125]
“Very well.”

[P126]
“Young Master,” Butler Kim said.

[P127]
“Don’t worry. I won’t go far.”

[P128]
“……Then I’ll follow at a distance.”

[P129]
Song nodded and slowly drew the weapon at his waist.

[P130]
“I suppose I can’t stop you doing that. Suit yourself.”

[P131]
“You—!”

[P132]
“Don’t misunderstand.”

[P133]
*Thud.*

[P134]
What Butler Kim feared did not happen. Song drove his weapon deep into the snow for them to see, and Choi started walking.

[P135]
*Crunch. Crunch.*

[P136]
Snow crumbled beneath their feet as they walked side by side.

[P137]
After a few steps, Song finally broke his silence.

[P138]
“There’s a secret area inside Ares Guild headquarters. Only a handful of people can enter.”

[P139]
“Are you referring to Area A?”

[P140]
“……!”

[P141]
Song’s eyes widened at the unexpected question.

[P142]
“I knew the area existed and what it was called,” Choi said calmly. “I couldn’t find out anything more.”

[P143]
“……Impressive. How did you learn even that?”

[P144]
“I put in more effort than you might imagine. What I need now isn’t praise, though. I need details. What does Area A have to do with my maternal grandfather’s safety?”

[P145]
“He’s there.”

[P146]
*Crunch.*

[P147]
Choi stopped dead at those two words. After a moment of silence, he began walking again.

[P148]
“You can’t be certain of that.”

[P149]
“Why do you say that?”

[P150]
“You were pushed out of the Ares Guild’s inner circle long ago, Regional Director.”

[P151]
“……That stings. But you’re right. I can’t be certain.”

[P152]
“I also can’t see why my maternal grandfather would be there. No—I can’t understand it.”

[P153]
“Why…”

[P154]
Song sighed softly.

[P155]
“Of course you can’t. No one knows what happened to him. Not even you.”

[P156]
“What are you—”

[P157]
Choi turned to him, questioning. Song’s next words stopped him cold.

[P158]
“It’s been more than twenty years since he lost consciousness.”

[P159]
“……!”

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). ## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.

- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.
